answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work: before an agent can join the market, it must complete a verifiable task whose difficulty rises with each new identity from the same hardware fingerprint. A flood of fake agents then faces a river of rising cost, not a free ride. Peers keep a lantern-lit registry of completed proofs, and an ivory-tower reputation score grows only from attested work, so sybils pay real compute for every extra face while honest agents pay once.
